 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ramachandra D. Huddar)

The appellant - NEKRTC, Raichur represented by its Divisional Controller, has questioned the judgment and award dated 20.11.2023 passed in MVC Nos.604/2021 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT, Raichur (for short, 'the Tribunal'), challenging the award on the ground of contributory negligence.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimants have not preferred any appeal being aggrieved by the said award passed by the Tribunal.
2. The parties herein are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the claimants before the Tribunal, that the claimants filed the petition seeking compensation on account of death of Nijananda in a road traffic accident that occurred on 23.11.2021 because of rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 - the driver of NEKRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-36/F-1454 owned by respondent No.2.

It is stated that the deceased was doing NC: 2024:KHC-K:6913-DB vegetable business during his lifetime and because of his untimely death, the claimants have suffered a lot both financially and mentally.
Therefore, the claimants be compensated on account of untimely death of Nijananda.
4. Before the Tribunal, both the respondents appeared.
They resisted the petition by filing detailed objection statement.
So far as respondent No.1 is concerned, he denied all the assertions and allegations made in the petition.
It is contended that, the deceased Nijananda was not holding effective driving license.
The said accident has taken place because of his rash and negligent driving of his motor cycle.
The claimants are not entitled for compensation.
Respondent No.1 was holding driving license and he was not negligent in driving the bus.
The claim of the claimants is exorbitant and excessive.
Similarly respondent No.2 has denied all the assertions made in the petition.
Thus, it is contended by both the respondents that, they are not liable to pay any amount of compensation as claimed in the claim petition.
Based on the rival pleadings of both the parties, the learned Tribunal framed relevant issues.
6. Before the Tribunal, to substantiate the case of the claimants, claimant No.1 entered witness box as PW-1 and got marked Exs.P-1 to P-14 and closed claimants' evidence.
So far as other claim petition is concerned, PW- 2 was examined.
Respondent No.1 was examined as RW- 1 and on behalf of respondents Exs.R1 to R16 were marked.

7. Learned Tribunal, on hearing the arguments and on evaluation of the evidence placed on record by both sides, allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.29,73,500/- under all the relevant heads.
The Tribunal has fixed liability on both the respondents but however respondent No.2 being the employer of respondent No.1 is made liable to pay the compensation amount.

sentences.text: Now the appellant - Corporation is before this Court on the ground that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the bus in causing the accident.
It was the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Therefore, now the appellant has challenged the award on the ground of negligence only.
So far as quantum of compensation awarded is concerned, the appellant has not challenged the same and no grounds are made out in appeal memo.

To prove the case of the claimants, they have produced various documents like CC of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, M.V.
report, postmortem report, charge sheet, etc.
They are marked as Exs.P-1 to P-7 before the Tribunal.
Learned counsel for the claimants made available the sketch of the scene of offence.
It is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that there was no rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.

But however, the learned counsel for the claimants submits that on reading the sketch so prepared by the police at the time of panchanama, it shows that, the rider and pillion rider of the motor cycle were on the left side of the road NC: 2024:KHC-K:6913-DB and the bus by crossing the middle of the road came towards the left side of the road and dashed against the motor cycle.
The sketch clearly shows that, how far the driver of the NEKRTC bus drove his bus without following the traffic rules and regulations.
The bus driver crossed the middle of the road and came to the extreme left side of the road where the motor cycle was moving and dashed against the motor cycle.
The sketch itself goes to establish that, the driver of the said bus was rash and negligent in driving the bus.
The drivers of the vehicle in case of accidents are the best witnesses to speak about the accident.
Their evidence would be the best evidence to know how and why the accident has taken place.

The panchanama and other documents produced by the claimants before the Tribunal and also the sketch made available by the learned counsel for the claimants clearly demonstrate that, the said accident has taken place because of rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver i.e.,
respondent No.1.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6913-DB 9.
The learned Tribunal, considering all these aspects, has clearly held that, the said accident has taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the bus.
We do not find any factual or legal error being committed by the Tribunal in coming to such a finding.
10. So far as the liability is concerned, because of the rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver, the accident has taken place.
Therefore, for the fault of the employee i.e., servant, the master is liable.
Therefore, under law of contract, both the respondents are held liable to pay the compensation.
However, respondent No.2 being the owner of the said bus, is liable to pay the compensation amount.
11. As stated supra, the appellant has not challenged the quantum of compensation and even the claimants have also not preferred any appeal.
Therefore, there cannot be any interference in the award passed by the Tribunal.

The appeal filed by the appellant lacks merit NC:
2024:KHC-K:6913-DB and is liable to be dismissed.

Accordingly, we pass the following:
ORDER The Divisional Controller vs Bhagyamma And Ors on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87994423/
